cases.name: Architecture selection — tabular data with tree baseline
cases.input: I want to train a deep learning model on my tabular dataset. Set up the architecture and training pipeline.
expected_behaviors: Recommends training a LightGBM/CatBoost baseline first before DL
Suggests TabularMLP with LayerNorm and GELU activations for tabular data
Provides argument parsing pattern with str_to_bool for boolean flags
Includes early stopping and learning rate scheduling in the training loop
Specifies GPU compute requirements (STANDARD_NC* SKUs)
should_not: Use BatchNorm for small batch sizes (<256)
Use store_true/store_false for boolean CLI arguments

cases.name: Optuna hyperparameter tuning with pruning
cases.input: Set up Optuna hyperparameter tuning for my PyTorch model on Azure ML.
expected_behaviors: Defines search spaces for learning rate (log-scale), batch size (categorical), dropout, and architecture depth
Uses TPESampler with MedianPruner for efficient search
Includes trial.report() and trial.should_prune() in the training loop
Sets reasonable trial budget (e.g., 50 trials with 2-hour timeout)
Logs Optuna best params and param importances to MLflow
should_not: Use grid search instead of Bayesian optimization
Omit pruning — running full epochs on bad trials wastes GPU time
Use linear scale for learning rate search

cases.name: Gradient diagnostics and regularization
cases.input: My model loss is NaN after a few epochs. Help me diagnose and fix the training instability.
expected_behaviors: Checks gradient norms for exploding gradients (max norm > 10)
Recommends gradient clipping with torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_
Suggests reducing learning rate by 10x as first remediation
Checks for vanishing gradients (min norm < 1e-8) and suggests GELU/LeakyReLU
Recommends adding LayerNorm if not already present
should_not: Suggest increasing learning rate when loss is NaN
Ignore the possibility of data issues (infinite values, missing targets)
Recommend removing dropout as a fix for NaN loss

cases.name: Model export for Azure ML inference pipeline
cases.input: My DL model is trained. How do I export it for the Azure ML inference pipeline?
expected_behaviors: Saves model as state_dict (not full model pickle)
Creates model_metadata.json with architecture config for reconstruction
Provides inference scoring script that loads config + state_dict
Uses torch.no_grad() context in inference
Handles device placement (cuda/cpu) in both training and inference
should_not: Hardcode device as 'cuda' in inference (must detect availability)
Forget to set model.eval() before inference

cases.name: Distributed training setup on AML multi-GPU
cases.input: I need to train my model across multiple GPUs on Azure ML compute.
expected_behaviors: Uses DDP (DistributedDataParallel) for single-node multi-GPU
Specifies torchrun command with AZUREML environment variables
Sets LOCAL_RANK and device per process
Mentions FSDP as alternative for models too large for single GPU
Configures instance_count > 1 for multi-node training
should_not: Use DataParallel (legacy, single-process) instead of DDP
Assume all AML compute instances have multiple GPUs
